title: Color picker with oversized results window

judgment.rationale: The reported Color Picker editor is much larger than its declared 440-by-380 logical size; display scaling and window sizing need a maintainer reproduction before choosing a resize policy.
evidence: PowerToys 0.102.3101.0 on Windows 10 22H2 build 19045.7807 reportedly opens a 1750-by-1100 result window.
The issue supplies a screenshot and says dragging the corners cannot resize it.

Current main src/modules/colorPicker/ColorPickerUI/ColorPickerXAML/ColorEditorWindow.xaml declares Width=440 and Height=380. This does not by itself explain the reported pixel dimensions or establish the monitor scale.
judgment.recommended_action: Compare editor physical bounds against logical size at several display scales before modifying initial size and minimum bounds.

proposed_fixes.title: Constrain Color Picker editor sizing to display work area
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A DPI conversion or minimum-size interaction may enlarge the editor beyond the intended logical size; the screenshot alone does not distinguish it from expected scaling.
plan: Trace ColorEditorWindow startup sizing and scale conversions, comparing physical bounds to the 440-by-380 XAML size.
Correct a duplicate scale conversion if reproduced; constrain startup/minimum bounds to the current monitor work area without hiding editor controls.
Test reopening and moving the editor across mixed-DPI displays before deciding whether user-resizable persistence is needed.
verification: Compare Windows 10 at multiple scaling factors and mixed-DPI monitors; verify visible controls and usable editor bounds.

confidence.rationale: A concrete size mismatch and source sizing boundary exist, but the reporter's DPI/topology and failing conversion are not yet established.

actions.label: Approve Constrain Color Picker editor sizing to display work area

reproduce.title: Verify reported Color Picker behavior
prerequisites: Use a Windows system supported by the tested PowerToys version.
steps: Open Color Picker, select a screen color and record the result editor's physical dimensions.
Repeat at 100%, 150% and 200% Windows display scaling, then after moving between differently scaled monitors.
Try corner resizing and record usable work area and actual editor bounds.
reproduce.expected_result: The result editor fits the available work area with readable content and no double-applied scaling.
